summary:
Mars Sandbox is an interactive 2D educational game created by Team F2Tech as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge. This game is aimed at 7 to 12-year-old kids who learn about the difficulties of exploring the Red Planet and creating a sustainable base on it.
Players create their own base on Mars, maintain balance of key resources, including oxygen, energy, water, and food supplies, and explore various parts of the planet by means of rovers. The goal of players is to operate their base for seven Martian days without being affected by external conditions.
Unlike other learning materials, Mars Sandbox provides young players with the opportunity to see the result of their actions. With the combination of all these factors, we aim to make studying space science easier, more interesting, and enjoyable for our players.
details:
Mars Sandbox is a 2D browser-based educational game made for children of ages between 7 and 12. We have created it for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in the framework of the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. We have thought up the game where children will get some experience in establishing and sustaining a base on Mars, and not learning about space missions from books and videos only.

The major objective of the game is to sustain operations of a Martian base for seven Martian sols - days. To do so, one needs to control four types of resources - oxygen, energy, water, and food. One can build various structures such as solar panels, oxygen producers, habitat, and greenhouse while making sure that their base has enough resources for operation. Each action will matter in the game since building structures, controlling supplies and conditions will influence the whole outpost.

Exploration is one more element of the game. It involves moving through an interactive map of Mars, finding new areas, and sending rovers to conduct an expedition in order to explore new terrain and find some resources. The game also features a technology tree which provides the ability to unlock new equipment and upgrades by solving scientific challenges. Additional difficulty includes Martian weather, temperature, and terrain. Interactive tutorial which lasts only a few minutes gives a hint on how to play the game.

We have chosen the sandbox format as we have wanted to provide children with the particular freedom of choices. Some strategy exists here and no linear plot exists in the game. Children can make decisions, see their effects and consequences, learn from their failures. In this way, such concepts as resource management, energy generation, and life support systems become easier to understand. Besides, the game provides problem-solving opportunities and promotes curiosity.

Our team worked out the game concept, its mechanics, educational component, interface, and user experience. Our focus was on the simplicity of the game while playing and understanding for children.

Scientific topics covered in this project include Martian geography, environmental conditions, energy production, and resources necessary for sustaining life on Mars. The sources related to this topic are NASA Mars Trek, NASA DONKI, and educational resources from the Canadian Space Agency.
